briefs.polymarket-5167210: The question asks whether Saudi Arabia's own armed forces carry out a qualifying air or surface-to-surface missile strike that impacts Yemen on 29 October 2026, Yemen Standard Time. On 13 October Saudi Arabia struck an oil depot near Sanaa and the coalition said it hit Houthi fuel sites in Sanaa, Hodeidah and Dhamar (https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/13/saudi-arabia-strikes-strategic-oil-depots-near-yemen-capital). On 18 October Houthi and Yemeni health sources reported a Saudi airstrike on a home in Saada killing at least nine people, which Al-Monitor labelled alleged (https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/10/saudi-coalition-houthis-trade-strikes-disruption-spreads; https://en.ypagency.net/408888). Al-Monitor said the Saudi-Houthi war reignited in July with repeated coalition air raids. On 16 October a Saudi deputy foreign minister said a Saudi request for talks with the Houthis in Oman had been refused. A diplomatic pause or ceasefire before 29 October would lower the chance of a qualifying strike; continued daily operations would raise it.
